headline: Antonelli masters the wet to win in Montréal
standfirst: Kimi Antonelli won the Canadian Grand Prix for Mercedes, finishing 10.768s ahead of Lewis Hamilton, with Max Verstappen completing the podium after 68 laps of Montreal.

sections.title: The start
sections.body: George Russell lined up first on the grid. Norris got the better launch and led the field across the line at the end of the opening lap. The biggest winner of the opening lap was Bearman, up 5 places to 11th.

sections.title: How it unfolded
sections.body: The lead changed hands 5 times. Laps led: Antonelli (46), Russell (21) and Norris (1). Antonelli took the lead for good on lap 30. The race ran green from start to finish.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Antonelli made 1 stop, running soft → medium tyres. The field made 34 pit stops in total; the quickest stationary time was 2.2s for Norris on lap 2. 8 of the top 10 finishers got home with one stop or fewer.

sections.title: Movers
sections.body: Lance Stroll made up the most ground, climbing 7 places from 22nd to 15th. Piastri went the other way, slipping from 4th to 11th. Timing recorded 243 on-track position changes, 20 of them by Piastri.

sections.title: Retirements
sections.body: Norris (lap 39), Perez (lap 40), Alonso (lap 24), Albon (lap 12) and Russell (lap 30) failed to finish. Lindblad did not take the start.

sections.title: Conditions and pace
sections.body: A damp track called for wet-weather tyres for part of the distance, although little rain fell during the race itself. Track temperature ranged from 17°C to 19°C, with air at 12–14°C. Kimi Antonelli set the fastest lap, a 1:14.210 on lap 68.
